Front: What problem does MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) retrieval fix?
Back: Plain top-k returns near-duplicate chunks (redundant). MMR balances relevance to the query against diversity from already-selected chunks (a lambda tradeoff), so you get varied-but-relevant context instead of five copies of the same passage.

Front: What does self-query retrieval do that semantic search can't?
Back: An LLM splits the natural-language query into a semantic search string + a structured METADATA filter (e.g. 'RAG papers after 2022' -> search 'RAG' + filter year>2022). Enforces hard constraints that pure embeddings can't. Requires metadata on the documents.

After retrieval, an LLM trims each chunk to only the query-relevant sentences and drops irrelevant chunks, producing a tighter, higher-signal context. Great for local models (small context window, slow inference); tradeoff is extra LLM calls.

Front: Why did residual depth + augmentation beat loss weighting on the ECG model?
Back: Depth raised the model's capacity ceiling and skip connections let the deeper net train (gradients flow); augmentation added effective data/variety for rare classes. Loss weighting only rebalances a FIXED model - it can't add capacity or data, so it shifts precision/recall but not macro-F1. (It is a ResNet / residual CNN, not an RNN.)

Front: Why does a beat-level random split inflate ECG scores vs a patient-wise split?
Back: Each person's ECG has an idiosyncratic waveform signature. A random split puts the same patient's beats in train AND test, so the model can shortcut by recognizing the person instead of learning generalizable arrhythmia features. A patient-wise (inter-patient/AAMI) split has all-new test patients, so scores drop to true generalization.

Front: How does focal loss differ from class-weighted cross-entropy?
Back: Focal loss weights by example DIFFICULTY, not class frequency: it multiplies CE by (1-p_t)^gamma, so easy/confident examples contribute ~0 and hard/misclassified ones keep near-full loss. Down-weights the flood of easy majority examples. Class weighting weights by rarity. They compose (alpha-balanced focal loss).

Front: Why does ensembling tend to beat any single model?
Back: Averaging models with INDEPENDENT (decorrelated) errors cancels the random mistakes while the shared correct signal reinforces - variance reduction. Requires diversity (different seeds/arch/data); averaging identical models does nothing. Mainly cuts variance, not bias.
